items.goal: On My orders, show each order's Date in the browser's own time zone, in the existing format MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss. Orders.razor renders each date as <time class="order-date" datetime="{UTC ISO-8601 round-trip, Kind forced to Utc}"> with the current UTC text as a fallback. A new src/WebApp/wwwroot/js/order-local-time.js, loaded in App.razor next to the other scripts, rewrites every such element into the local date and time (24-hour, zero-padded month/day/hour/min/sec). It runs on load, after Blazor enhanced navigation (enhancedload) and when streaming or OrdersRefreshOnStatusChange inserts or replaces rows (MutationObserver), without converting a value twice. Order number, total and status stay unchanged. No scenario fits: the verifier signs in as alice, places an order (Explorer 45L Backpack), then opens My orders with the browser time zone set to America/Chicago and to Asia/Tokyo.
items.modelReason: Small but needs care with the Blazor streaming and enhanced-navigation lifecycle and with UTC handling.
items.verifyReason: Visible behavior that depends on the browser's time zone; a verifier must set the browser time zone and read the page.

subject: implementer
reason: Order dates are stored as UTC (DateTime.UtcNow, timestamptz), rendered as a round-trip UTC instant in <time datetime>, and converted in the browser to MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss local time, including the date, which meets Expected for every row; streamed rows and Nav.Refresh status updates are re-converted by the idempotent MutationObserver. The change stays inside WebApp and follows the existing wwwroot/js script pattern.

items.reason: The MutationObserver watches all of document.body (childList, subtree, characterData) on every page, so any page mutation (e.g. chat widgets) schedules a querySelectorAll scan even on pages without order dates.
items.fix: Optional: scope the observer to the .orders container, or start it only when a time[data-local-time] element exists.

items.reason: The enhancedload hook with a 150 ms setTimeout retry loop looks redundant, because the body-wide MutationObserver already fires on the DOM changes enhanced navigation makes.
items.fix: Optional: drop hookEnhancedNav, or keep it with a comment saying why it is needed.

items.title: In America/Chicago an order placed at 15:08:50 UTC shows 11/16/2026 09:08:50
covers: Expected: Date in the browser's time zone, 11/16/2026 09:08:50 in America/Chicago
items.reason: The ticket's first Expected bullet is the core of the bug: a Chicago shopper must see 09:08:50, not the UTC 15:08:50. Seeding a fixed OrderDate makes the expected text exact; e2e is the only layer where the browser's time zone applies.

items.title: In Asia/Tokyo the same order shows the next day, 11/17/2026 00:08:50
covers: Expected: same order shows 11/17/2026 00:08:50 in Asia/Tokyo; the date follows the time zone
items.reason: The second Expected bullet requires the date, not only the time, to follow the browser's zone; a fix that shifted only hours, or one fixed to the server's zone, would show 11/16. Separate from TC-01 because it checks a different zone and a calendar-day change on the same order.

items.title: In America/Chicago every order on the page shows its local date and time, across DST and a previous-day rollover
covers: Expected: every other order on the page is shown the same way
Expected: same format as today (MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss)
items.reason: The third Expected bullet says every order is converted, not only the newest; a fix that touched only the first row or applied one fixed offset would pass TC-01 but fail here. Order 2 is in daylight time (UTC-5) and order 3 rolls back to the previous day, so a hard-coded -6 offset or a time-only shift shows wrong values. Order 2's 16:05:07 also checks the 24-hour, zero-padded format.

items.title: In Asia/Tokyo orders one second either side of local midnight show different dates
covers: Expected: the date follows the browser's time zone too
items.reason: The date-follows-zone rule has a boundary at local midnight: 14:59:59 UTC is still 16 November in Tokyo and 15:00:00 UTC is 17 November. An off-by-one in the offset or a conversion that rounds or drops seconds would put both on the same day. Same layer and scenario as TC-02 because only the browser applies the zone.

items.title: Order number, total and status are unchanged by the date conversion
covers: Expected: the order number, total and status are unchanged
items.reason: The ticket requires the other columns to stay as they are; the fix rewrites text inside the rows on the client, so a selector that is too broad could rewrite or blank another cell. Run in Asia/Tokyo, where every date changes, so any spill-over into other cells is visible.

items.title: Bug report replay: an order placed through the UI in America/Chicago shows the browser clock's time on My orders
covers: Acceptance criteria: repeating the steps matches Expected
Expected: Date is the date and time the order was placed in the browser's time zone
items.reason: The acceptance criterion is to repeat the reported steps: an order placed now, through checkout, then My orders opened from the site's navigation. This catches what the seeded cases cannot: the real OrderDate written by Ordering.API and the page reached by Blazor enhanced navigation rather than a full load. The exact second is not controllable, so the check is a time window from the browser clock.
